title: Field action equivalence with normalized geometric derived sections
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with the Krull topology. Work in compatible universes making the sites small [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a profinite set $P$ write $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$, over its finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor]. Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring, put $R_T=p_T^*R$, and use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $\mathcal A_G(R)$ mean internal $R$-modules with an action of the condensed group $P\mapsto C(P,G)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

There is an exact additive equivalence $E_R:\operatorname{Mod}_{R_s}\simeq\mathcal A_G(R)$ with $(E_RN)(P)=\Gamma(\bar s[P],N|_{\bar s[P]})$. The action comes from the $k$-automorphisms of $k^s$. Its derived equivalence is t-exact. For every coefficient map $R\to R'$, it identifies scalar restriction, ordinary and derived scalar extension, their adjunction units and counits, with those in the action categories. In particular it identifies the canonical coefficient projection for a structure morphism $a:X\to s$ with the morphism $\beta:R'\otimes^L_R\mathcal K_R(M)\to\mathcal K_{R'}(R'_X\otimes^L_{R_X}M)$ for the functors $\mathcal K$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent], defined as the transpose under the derived scalar adjunction $R'\otimes^L_R-\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ of $\mathcal K_R(M)\xrightarrow{\mathcal K_R(\eta_M)}\mathcal K_R(\operatorname{Res}(R'_X\otimes^L_{R_X}M))\to\operatorname{Res}\mathcal K_{R'}(R'_X\otimes^L_{R_X}M)$, where $\eta_M$ is the derived scalar-extension unit and the second arrow is the canonical comparison of $\mathcal K$ with the exact scalar restriction, and $D(E_R)Ra_*M\cong\mathcal K_R(M)$ canonically for every qcqs $k$-scheme $X$ and $M\in D(R_X)$.

Let $u:X^s=X\times_k k^s\to X$ and let $p_{X^s}$ be the structural geometric morphism from its pro-etale topos to the condensed topos. Forgetting the $G$-action identifies $\mathcal K_R(M)$ with $Rp_{X^s*}u^*M$. Under this identification the forgotten coefficient projection is exactly
$$R'\otimes_R^L Rp_{X^s*}u^*M\longrightarrow Rp_{X^s*}(R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}u^*M),$$
the counit-adjoint projection map. These identifications commute with coefficient restriction, input morphisms and canonical shifts. Forgetting the action is exact and conservative, also on the derived categories.

If $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with its norm topology and $R(P)=C(P,E)$, $E_R$ restricts to an equivalence between finite-rank lisse $R_s$-modules [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] and finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector spaces $W$ with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action, realized by $P\mapsto C(P,W)$. Rank zero and trivial $G$ are included.

source.place: Example 4.1.10 (field site); Definition 6.8.3 and Proposition 6.8.4 (finite-field lisse modules). Agent-formulated ordinary derived and coefficient normalization of that presentation; exact combined reference WANTED.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-sfb-field-profinite-galois-site], the qcqs field site is $\mathbf{Prof}_G$, with finite jointly surjective covers, and is dense in $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. All sites and comma categories are small in the coefficient universe, so the limits required by [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] exist for sets and abelian groups. Restriction therefore identifies their sheaf categories. Under this presentation, $\bar s[P]$ is $G\times P$ with left translation and $s[P]$ is the trivial $G$-set $P$, naturally in $P$.

The free objects form another dense full subsite: $G\times S\to S$, $(g,x)\mapsto gx$, is an equivariant continuous surjection. An equivariant map $G\times T\to G\times P$ is uniquely $(g,t)\mapsto(gb(t),f(t))$. Composing $(f,b)$ with $(h,c)$ gives $(fh,c\,h^*b)$; such a finite family covers precisely when the underlying $f$'s jointly cover. Thus this is the action site of [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. The density equivalence of [lem-pc-fppf-dense-sheaf-equivalence] and that action-site equivalence give $E:\operatorname{Sh}(s_{\mathrm{proet}})\simeq\operatorname{Cond}^{\underline G}$, with $(EF)(P)=F(\bar s[P])$. Right translation on the free factor induces the stated action, with exactly the displayed composition convention.

For trivial $P$, the cover $G\times P\to P$ has kernel pair $G\times G\times P$. Its sheaf equalizer says that $F(P)$ consists of the sections of $EF(P)$ fixed after every profinite base change: the two arrows are restriction and the action. Consequently the direct image $p_{s*}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point] becomes invariants. Its left adjoint becomes trivial inflation, the inverse image of $p_G$ in [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. The comparison is the unique adjoint comparison, including units and counits. It preserves products and hence the addition, multiplication and unit of every ring $R$. Thus $E(R_s)=R$ with trivial action, naturally in ring maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] to this ringed equivalence and [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation] to identify its module category with $\mathcal A_G(R)$. This gives the exact additive $E_R$, with the required section formula and scalar action. Here [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] identifies internal modules with section-ring module sheaves without altering sections or restrictions; its sheafification hypotheses hold for these small abelian-sheaf sites and their usual sheaf tensor.

By [lem-sfb-internal-action-site-presentation], forgetting the action creates kernels and cokernels and detects the zero module. It is therefore exact and conservative. On complexes it commutes with cohomology; if a derived morphism becomes invertible, its cone has zero forgotten cohomology, hence zero cohomology, so the morphism was invertible. The termwise derived equivalence supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-presentation-transport] is t-exact: exactness gives $H^n(D(E_R)K)=E_RH^n(K)$, and the same holds for its inverse. No bound on $n$ or on $G$ is involved.

For $\varphi:R\to R'$, the formula for $E_R$ commutes with scalar restriction: only the action of $R(P)$ changes by $\varphi_P$. Ordinary extension is left adjoint to this restriction by [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], on both presentations. The resulting adjoint comparison identifies the two extension functors and their units and counits: both transpose a map by $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ and evaluate a scalar-linear map by $r'\otimes m\mapsto r'f(m)$. These formulas are valid locally and hence after module sheafification. In particular the transported equivalence is strong monoidal, with the balanced tensor comparison sending local pure tensors to the same pure tensors, and preserving the regular module.

Regard $\varphi$ as a ringed-topos morphism with identity underlying topos. Its module direct image is exact scalar restriction. The K-flat pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] is derived scalar extension, with the adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Under a ringed equivalence, K-flatness is preserved: the tensor identification of step 5 and the exact inverse equivalence identify tensoring with every acyclic complex on the two sides. Hence the ordinary pure-tensor comparison on K-flat representatives gives the derived extension comparison. The derived units and counits agree, since both adjunction bijections are obtained from the same chain-level scalar transposition by localization. This proves all scalar-adjunction assertions for arbitrary, possibly non-flat, $R\to R'$.

proof.text: Let $a:X\to s$. On underlying sections [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] gives $(a_*M)(V)=M(X\times_s V)$. In the inverse-limit construction of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor], base change commutes with this limit: maps to either side specify the same compatible maps to the finite disjoint copies. This gives $X\times_s\bar s[P]=X^s[P]$, with all restriction maps. Thus $E_Ra_*M$ is the underived equivariant geometric section functor whose total right derived functor is $\mathcal K_R$ in [lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent]. On a K-injective $I$ representing $M$, both $D(E_R)Ra_*M$ and $\mathcal K_R(M)$ are represented by the identical complex $E_Ra_*I$. This is a canonical isomorphism in the unbounded derived category, by the resolution definition in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

source.place: Paragraph (3), geometric direct image before arithmetic descent

proof.text: Write $v:\bar s\to s$ and $h=h_{\bar s}$. The site localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the slice at $\bar s$ with $\bar s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. In the free-object presentation a map $G\times P\to G$ is $(g,p)\mapsto gb(p)$. It is isomorphic over $G$ to the projection by the automorphism $(g,p)\mapsto(gb(p),p)$; maps between these projections are just continuous maps of $P$. Slice restriction therefore sends $N$ to $P\mapsto N(\bar s[P])$, forgetting its action. The coefficient identification of step 3 restricts to $R_{\bar s}$; for any condensed $R$ its pullback identification is [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Thus forgetting $E_RN$ is the module restriction $v^*N$, followed by the field presentation for $\bar s$ (whose group is trivial).

Apply [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison] to $a$ and the target sheaf $h_{\bar s}$. Its inverse image is $h_{X^s}$ and its source slice is $X^s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The ring on each slice is the restriction of the original ring, identified with its pulled-back coefficient by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. That comparison gives $v^*Ra_*M\cong Ra_{s*}u^*M$, preserving the counit and the canonical tensor comparison, where $a_s:X^s\to\bar s$. Over $\bar s$, the presentation in step 1 is the profinite site itself, and $p_{\bar s}$ is its equivalence with the condensed topos. Since $p_{X^s}=p_{\bar s}a_s$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies this object with $Rp_{X^s*}u^*M$. On a K-injective $I$, the slice comparison is the actual restriction identity and $u^*I$ is K-injective, as the cited slice theorem states. This proves the requested derived-object identification, rather than only its cohomology consequences.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; unbounded mate refinement as in the cited slice node

proof.text: The comparisons with scalar restriction needed below are the canonical ones, including for a non-flat coefficient map. Indeed the two composites consisting of structure direct image and scalar restriction are the same ringed-topos direct image. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the two factorizations. This gives $Ra_{*,R}\operatorname{Res}_X\cong\operatorname{Res}_sRa_{*,R'}$; use step 7 for $\mathcal K$. Its normalization is the comparison computed on resolutions in that node, not an arbitrary automorphism of the resulting derived object. In particular all occurrences of scalar restriction in the following transposition use this same comparison.

source.place: Paragraph (3), scalar-restriction comparison for ordinary derived geometric sections

proof.text: Set $S_T=R'_T\otimes^L_{R_T}-$, let $\eta_M:M\to\operatorname{Res}_X S_XM$ be its unit, and let $\rho$ denote step 10. Define $\beta$ to be the scalar-adjunction transpose of $\mathcal K_R(M)\xrightarrow{\mathcal K_R(\eta_M)}\mathcal K_R(\operatorname{Res}_X S_XM)\xrightarrow{\rho}\operatorname{Res}\mathcal K_{R'}(S_XM)$. On the field side the same transpose defines $\chi:S_sRa_{*,R}M\to Ra_{*,R'}S_XM$. It is the coefficient projection: under $a_{R'}^*\dashv Ra_{*,R'}$, its adjunct is $a_{R'}^*S_sRa_{*,R}M\cong S_Xa_R^*Ra_{*,R}M\xrightarrow{S_X\varepsilon_M}S_XM$. To check the equality, apply [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] to the square of ringed topoi $(X,R'_X)\to(X,R_X)\to(s,R_s)$ and $(X,R'_X)\to(s,R'_s)\to(s,R_s)$, whose composites are the same ringed morphism: the composition comparison $\rho$ of step 10 is the conjugate of the derived pullback comparison $a_{R'}^*S_s\cong S_Xa_R^*$, with the displayed counit equation. Transposing the scalar unit first and then $a^*\dashv Ra_*$, this counit equation and the unit-counit cancellation leave exactly $S_X\varepsilon_M$. This is precisely the defining formula in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. By steps 6–7 the two scalar-adjunction transposes agree under $D(E_R)$, so $D(E_{R'})\chi=\beta$ under the stated identifications.

source.place: Paragraph (3), normalized coefficient projection; explicit two-adjunction transpose computation

proof.text: Restrict the last counit formula to the slices at $\bar s$ and $X^s$. The counit equation of [lem-sbc-ringed-topos-sheaf-slice-derived-comparison] takes its $\varepsilon$ to the counit for $a_s$, while its K-flat comparison takes scalar tensor to scalar tensor. The equivalence $p_{\bar s}$ then leaves the same formula for $p_{X^s}$, by the adjunction-normalized composition of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] (both geometric coefficient pullbacks are exact, by [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], and $p_{\bar s}$ is an exact equivalence). Thus forgotten $\beta$ is the adjunct of $p_{X^s}^*(R'\otimes_R^LRp_{X^s*}u^*M)\cong R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}p_{X^s}^*Rp_{X^s*}u^*M\to R'_{X^s}\otimes^L_{R_{X^s}}u^*M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] this is exactly the displayed counit-adjoint projection; its $R$-linear form there (adjoint under $p_{X^s,R}^*\dashv Rp_{X^s*,R}$, with $P=R'$) is the scalar restriction of this $R'$-linear adjunct followed by the composition comparison with $\operatorname{Res}$, by the conjugacy of [lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction] applied to $p_{X^s}$ as in step 11. This establishes equality of the specified morphisms.

source.place: Tag 04IF, lemma-localize-morphism-ringed-topoi; normalized derived counit square

proof.text: Every comparison above is induced by restriction, an adjunction comparison, or the natural derived slice/composition comparison. Hence it commutes with input morphisms. For coefficient restriction the ordinary squares are identity on sections and the derived comparisons in step 10 are the canonical composition comparisons; the cocycle of [lem-pur-ringed-derived-composition-cocycle] identifies the two ways round every such square. Termwise exact equivalences and restrictions commute with shifts. The remaining right derived functors have the canonical shifts of [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]; their units and counits commute with them by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. The coefficient projection commutes with shifts in $M$ by [lem-sfb-ringed-projection-first-shift]. Therefore the object identifications and the specified morphisms have all asserted naturality and shift compatibility.

source.place: Paragraph (3), naturality, coefficient restriction and canonical shifts

proof.text: Now take $R(P)=C(P,E)$ for finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. If $N$ is lisse in [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], its pullback to $\bar s$ is locally free. The profinite presentation of [lem-sfb-field-profinite-galois-site] supplies a nonempty profinite member $P$ of a trivializing cover of $*$. Choose $x\in P$. Restricting that free chart along $x:*\to P$ makes the underlying condensed module of $E_RN$ free of some finite rank $n$. Put $W=E^n$ with its product norm topology; coordinatewise continuous functions give $R(P)^n=C(P,W)$ for every profinite $P$. Conversely a module with this underlying form is free after pullback to the covering $\bar s\to s$, hence lisse. The local-free condition is preserved here because a ringed equivalence and slice restriction preserve finite direct sums and the regular module. For a given finite-dimensional norm-topological $W$, a basis identifies it homeomorphically with $E^n$: the linear identification and its inverse are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous].

source.place: Definition 6.8.3 and Example 4.1.10; direct split-cover argument over the separably closed field

proof.text: In a free basis, an internal action on $R^n$ is exactly a continuous representation. Apply its operation over the profinite test object $G$ to $\operatorname{id}_G\in C(G,G)$ and to each constant basis vector. The $n^2$ resulting coordinates belong to $R(G)=C(G,E)$ and define a continuous matrix-valued function $A:G\to\operatorname{Mat}_n(E)$. For $g:P\to G$, naturality says the action matrix is $A\circ g$; by $R(P)$-linearity this determines the action on every section. The action laws give $A(1)=1$ and $A(gh)=A(g)A(h)$, so its values are invertible. Thus $G\times E^n\to E^n$ is continuous, being a finite sum of products of these continuous coordinates with the vector coordinates. Conversely a continuous linear $G$-action gives exactly these operations on continuous-function sections. These two constructions are inverse without a discrete-topology substitution.

source.place: Example 4.1.10 and Definition 6.8.3; explicit matrix reconstruction for the field case

proof.text: A morphism $R^n\to R^m$ is determined by its values on the constant basis at $*$; its matrix has entries in $R(*)=E$ and acts pointwise on $C(P,E)^n$. It commutes with the internal action exactly when that matrix intertwines $A(g)$ for every $g$. Every such finite-dimensional linear map is continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], whose completeness and Hausdorff hypotheses hold for the finite normed extension $E$ and the finite-dimensional normed spaces here. This proves full faithfulness as well as the essential surjectivity in steps 14–15. The empty matrix gives rank zero; when $G=1$, all actions are trivial. For arbitrary condensed $R$, including the zero ring, steps 1–13 use only ringed sheaf and adjunction constructions and impose no additional coefficient hypothesis.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q01-b7519026b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item: statement and all 16 steps. I checked every cited node's statement, Bhatt–Scholze Ex. 4.1.10 (pp. 27–28) and blueprint main-20261015 direct-images paragraph (3). The statement is byte-identical to the NV-era copy and it is a first split (no repair note, no new nodes). There is no SGA source, no cycle, and no duplicate in the DAG (I checked the profinite-algcl invariants comparison, the exc G-module core and the global-descent node). Checks that held: steps 1–10 (free-orbit subsite = action site with composition (fh, c·h^*b); fully-fixed equalizer, so p_s^* = trivial inflation; exact conservative forgetting; K-flat preservation with no flatness of R→R'; E_R a_* = equivariant geometric sections on K-injectives; the slice comparison with A = h_{s̄}). Steps 13–16 also hold: lisse ⇔ finite free via a point of a profinite chart; the internal action on R^n ⇔ continuous representation by A = action of id_G; Hom = E-matrices. Two repairable faults, both fixed. (1) B3: the statement names 'the scalar-adjunction transpose defining β for K in lem-sfb-condensed-galois-global-descent', but that node does not define β. I wrote the explicit definition into the statement, the same formula as the parent's β_R; this clarifies, it does not weaken. (2) C1/C4: step 11's 'unit-counit cancellation' and step 12's identification of the R-linear projection α of ringed-projection-mate-exact with the R'-linear adjunct both need the step-10 composition comparison ρ to be the conjugate of the derived pullback comparison a_{R'}^*S_s ≅ S_X a_R^*. No cited node says this: derived-composition-adjunction-normalization needs exact left adjoints, and S is not exact. I cited lem-sfb-ringed-comparison-tensor-adjunction ('c is the conjugate of θ', for any commuting square of ringed topoi with no exactness assumed) in steps 11 and 12. I added it to proof_deps and to split_report.tool_uses (it belongs to another unit and is a generic mate fact) and checked that it does not reach the item. I accept the 15 declared tool uses.
